scenes.name: hook
scenes.text: A hard little corn kernel suddenly explodes into a fluffy white snack. What makes popcorn pop?

scenes.name: inside
scenes.text: Each kernel has a hard outer shell, with starch and a little water trapped inside.

scenes.name: heat
scenes.text: As you heat it, the water turns to steam, but the strong shell won't let it escape.

scenes.name: pressure
scenes.text: Pressure inside rises to several times normal air pressure, while the starch turns soft and gooey.

scenes.name: pop
scenes.text: At around one hundred and eighty degrees, the shell bursts. The steam expands and puffs the starch into foam.

scenes.name: set
scenes.text: The foam cools in a split second and sets into the crunchy shape we eat.

scenes.name: duds
scenes.text: Kernels that don't pop usually have a cracked shell or too little water, so pressure can't build.

scenes.name: outro
scenes.text: Water, heat, pressure, pop. Follow for more on how things really work.
